description: The mechanics, economics and risks of decentralised finance and digital assets: token standards, automated market makers, lending, stablecoins, central bank digital currencies, oracles, exploits, custody and regulation. Students build simulated pools, lending markets and attacks in code, replay real failure patterns and write risk assessments.
modelledOn: Harvey, Ramachandran and Santoro, DeFi and the Future of Finance
Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten, Miller and Goldfeder, Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies
Bank for International Settlements, Central bank digital currency reports and principles
outcomes: Implement and test token contracts and explain token standards, allowances and common design pitfalls.
Derive the pricing, slippage and impermanent loss of constant-product market makers and simulate liquidity provision.
Model overcollateralised lending, liquidations and stablecoin stability mechanisms, and identify when they fail.
Compare central bank digital currency designs with mobile money and cross-border payment systems in an African setting.
Analyse oracle manipulation, front-running and contract exploits, and propose defences and audit tests.
Assess custody, market structure, regulatory, tax and portfolio risk for a digital-asset product.

units.title: Ledgers, keys and execution
topics: Consensus recap: proof of work, proof of stake, finality and reorganisations
Account-based versus UTXO ledgers; transactions, fees and gas
Digital signatures, wallets, key derivation and seed phrases
The EVM execution model: storage, memory, calls and events
Tokens versus coins; why value is recorded on a shared ledger

units.title: Token standards and smart contracts
topics: ERC-20: balances, allowances, approve and transferFrom pitfalls
Non-fungible and multi-token standards (ERC-721, ERC-1155) and metadata
Contract design: state machines, access control and upgradeable proxies
Token economics: supply schedules, vesting, inflation and governance tokens
Testing contracts: unit tests, invariants and property-based fuzzing
Gas costs and optimisation

units.title: Automated market makers and liquidity pools
topics: Order books versus automated market makers
Constant-product pricing x*y=k: swap formula, slippage and price impact
Liquidity provision, pool shares, fees and the derivation of impermanent loss
Concentrated liquidity and stable-swap invariants
Arbitrage, price convergence and the idea of maximal extractable value

units.title: Lending, stablecoins and derivatives
topics: Overcollateralised lending: collateral factor, health factor and liquidation
Interest-rate models driven by pool utilisation
Stablecoin designs: fiat-backed, crypto-collateralised and algorithmic; depeg case studies
On-chain perpetual futures, funding rates and options
Flash loans: atomic borrowing and legitimate uses

units.title: Central bank digital currencies and payments
topics: CBDC design choices: retail versus wholesale, account-based versus token-based, two-tier architecture
Pilots in Africa (eNaira, eCedi) and their link to mobile money
Privacy, programmability and offline payments
Cross-border settlement and pan-African payment interoperability
Monetary-policy effects and bank disintermediation risk

units.title: Oracles, front-running and exploit analysis
topics: Oracles: price feeds, time-weighted averages and decentralised oracle networks
Front-running, sandwich attacks, private mempools and transaction ordering
Reentrancy, integer errors and access-control bugs in classic exploits
Flash-loan price-manipulation attacks, step by step
Bridge failures and key compromise
Auditing: static analysis, fuzzing, invariant tests and writing a post-mortem

units.title: Custody, exchanges and market structure
topics: Custody models: self-custody, custodial, multi-signature and multi-party computation
Centralised exchanges: matching engines, proof of reserves and collapse case studies
Market microstructure: spreads, depth, wash trading and manipulation
On-ramps and peer-to-peer markets in Ghana and Nigeria
Tokenised real-world assets

units.title: Regulation, tax and risk
topics: Regulatory frameworks: securities versus commodities, licensing, travel rule, KYC and AML; African regulatory approaches
Tax treatment of trading gains, staking income and airdrops
Risk taxonomy and quantification: smart contract, market, liquidity, counterparty and regulatory risk; value at risk for a crypto portfolio
Governance and decentralised autonomous organisations
Capstone: a protocol or product risk assessment report

schedule.title: Ledgers, keys and the execution model
schedule.exercise: Compare an account-based and a UTXO ledger for the same five payments, then explain how a signature proves ownership and why a lost seed phrase cannot be recovered.

tasks.title: Step a small proof-of-work chain through a fork and a reorganisation and note which transactions return to the pool
Generate a key pair, sign a payment message, verify it, then alter one byte and show the signature check fails
Build a small ledger that supports both account balances and UTXO transfers, and detect a double spend attempted in each model

schedule.title: Writing tokens
schedule.exercise: Specify the functions and events of a simple fungible token, then trace the allowance race condition between approve and transferFrom and explain the safer pattern.

tasks.title: Implement an ERC-20 style token in code with balances, transfer, approve and transferFrom, and pass a test list of 12 cases
Add a non-fungible token registry with unique ids, owner lookup and metadata hashes, and test that duplicate minting is rejected
Add owner-only minting and a pause switch to the token, then show an unauthorised call fails and a proxy-style upgrade keeps balances

schedule.title: Token economics, testing and gas
schedule.exercise: Design the supply and vesting schedule of a cooperative's governance token for 1000 members and test three invariants, such as total supply equal to the sum of balances.

tasks.title: Plot the circulating supply of a token with a 4-year linear vesting cliff and a halving emission and read the inflation rate in year 3
Write an invariant test that runs 10000 random transfers and approvals and checks that total supply never changes
Count storage writes and loop iterations in two implementations of a batch transfer and pick the cheaper one with a gas estimate

schedule.title: Constant-product markets
schedule.exercise: Price a swap in a pool with 1000 token A and 1000 token B, compute slippage for trades of 1, 10 and 100 units and compare with an order book of equal depth.

tasks.title: Compute the output, fee and slippage of three swaps against a pool of 1000 and 1000 tokens using the x*y=k rule
Simulate an order book and a constant-product pool receiving the same 200 random trades and compare average execution price
Code a swap function with a fee and a minimum-output check, then show a large trade moves the price along the curve

schedule.title: Liquidity provision and arbitrage
schedule.exercise: Derive impermanent loss as a function of the price ratio, evaluate whether fee income would have covered it for a stable pair and a volatile pair over 30 days.

tasks.title: Plot impermanent loss against price ratio from 0.25 to 4 and read off the loss when one asset doubles
Simulate a liquidity provider in a pool over 90 days of random prices and compare final value with simply holding, net of fees
Create two pools quoting different prices, write an arbitrage routine that trades between them and show both prices converge

schedule.title: Lending markets and liquidation
schedule.exercise: Set parameters for a lending pool of cedi-backed stablecoins and a volatile collateral asset, and test how a 30 percent price fall triggers liquidations and bad debt.

tasks.title: Compute the health factor of five borrowers from collateral value, debt and liquidation threshold and mark who can be liquidated
Plot a kinked utilisation interest-rate curve and compute borrower and lender rates at 50, 80 and 95 percent utilisation
Simulate 100 borrowers through a sudden 40 percent collateral price fall and measure liquidations, bad debt and the effect of a lower liquidation bonus

schedule.title: Stablecoins, derivatives and flash loans
schedule.exercise: Compare a reserve-backed stablecoin, a crypto-collateralised one and an algorithmic one under a bank-run scenario, identifying the feedback loop that makes the last unstable.

tasks.title: Simulate an algorithmic stablecoin paired with a volatile token through a demand shock and plot the peg until it breaks or recovers
Compute the funding payments of a perpetual future for a trader holding 10 times leverage over 7 days of given rates
Write a flash loan that borrows, trades and repays in one transaction and show it reverts when the profit is not enough

schedule.title: Central bank digital currencies
schedule.exercise: Design a retail digital cedi: choose account or token, the intermediary model, privacy and offline rules and the holding limit, then defend how it coexists with mobile money.

tasks.title: Draw the two-tier architecture of a retail CBDC showing the central bank, intermediaries, wallets and ledger, with the flow of one payment
Compute the deposit outflow from banks if households shift 10 percent of balances into CBDC and the effect of a holding cap
Work through a scenario on a low-adoption CBDC pilot, choose interventions with agents and mobile money operators, and score against a rubric

schedule.title: Oracles and transaction ordering
schedule.exercise: Show how a lending protocol using a single pool price can be manipulated in one block, and compare a spot oracle with a time-weighted average price.

tasks.title: Implement a time-weighted average price oracle over 20 blocks and compare it with the spot price during a one-block price spike
Build a mempool with a victim swap and a sandwiching attacker, compute the attacker profit and the victim's extra slippage
Exploit a reentrancy flaw in a simple vault contract by recursive withdrawal, then fix it with a checks-effects-interactions pattern

schedule.title: Attacks and audits
schedule.exercise: Replay a flash-loan manipulation attack step by step on a simulated lending pool, then write a one-page post-mortem naming the root cause, the loss, and the fix.

tasks.title: Execute a flash-loan price manipulation against a simulated lending market and report the attacker's profit and the pool's loss
Investigate a bridge-hack scenario by reading logs and key access records, identify how the signers were compromised and decide the response
Fuzz a staking contract with random calls, find the input that breaks a funds-conservation invariant and write the failing test

schedule.title: Custody, exchanges and market structure
schedule.exercise: Select a custody scheme for a savings group holding digital assets, then evaluate an exchange's proof-of-reserves report and market quality from a depth chart.

tasks.title: Implement a 2-of-3 multi-signature approval for withdrawals and show that one stolen key cannot move funds
Compute the spread and depth at 1 percent from a given order book snapshot and detect wash trades in a short trade log
Audit a scenario exchange's liabilities against its reserves, decide whether it is solvent and choose the customer communication

schedule.title: Regulation, tax and portfolio risk
schedule.exercise: Classify five token products under a securities test, compute tax on a year of trades and staking rewards, and estimate the one-day 95 percent value at risk of a three-asset portfolio.

tasks.title: Calculate taxable gains using first-in-first-out for a ledger of 12 buys, sells and staking rewards in cedis
Compute one-day 95 percent historical and parametric value at risk for a portfolio of three assets with given returns
Advise a mobile-money firm entering digital-asset custody in a regulatory scenario, choosing licensing, know-your-customer and reporting steps

schedule.title: Governance and capstone risk assessment
schedule.exercise: Write and present a risk assessment of a lending or exchange protocol, covering contract, oracle, market, governance and regulatory risk, with a quantified stress test and mitigations.

tasks.title: Simulate a governance vote with token-weighted voting and a whale, and measure how many voters decide the outcome
Run a stress test on a protocol model with a 50 percent price crash and a 3-day oracle delay, reporting insolvency and recovery
Present the protocol risk assessment to a scenario board and answer challenges, scored on completeness, quantification and recommended controls
